vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-gmail-reply
Version: 1.0.11

The skill bundle contains documentation (SKILL.md) for a Gmail reply functionality using a 'gws' CLI tool. It defines standard parameters for email operations such as message IDs, attachments, and recipient fields, and lacks any executable code or suspicious instructions that would indicate malicious intent or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it simply delegates Gmail reply operations to an existing 'gws' CLI and asks for no extra environment variables or installs, but it relies on external auth/config (gws-shared) which you should review before use.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Gmail reply) match the declared runtime requirement (the 'gws' CLI). No unrelated binaries or env vars are requested, so the capability aligns with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs use of the 'gws' CLI to construct/send replies (including attachments, html, draft, dry-run flags). It delegates auth, global flags, and security rules to ../gws-shared/SKILL.md — that external file controls authentication and policy. Review that file (or the output of 'gws generate-skills') because auth behavior and any additional scope come from it; the skill itself does not instruct broad system access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec. Nothing is written to disk by the skill itself; runtime risk is limited to invoking the existing 'gws' binary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No env vars are declared by this skill, which is reasonable because authentication is expected to be handled by the 'gws' CLI or the shared gws-shared SKILL.md. However, that means the CLI's stored credentials (OAuth tokens or config) will be used — verify those credentials and their Gmail scopes are appropriate (e.g., send-only vs full mailbox).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill doesn't request persistent system changes. It does reference potentially generating shared config via 'gws generate-skills', which can create files; inspect any generated files before trusting them.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a thin wrapper that runs the local 'gws' CLI to reply to Gmail messages; the skill itself contains no code or credentials. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the 'gws' binary on your system is from a trusted source and check its version/release page; 2) Inspect ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (or the files created by 'gws generate-skills') to see how authentication is handled and what Gmail scopes/tokens are used; 3) Test with --dry-run and/or --draft and avoid attaching sensitive files until you're confident; 4) If you share your machine, remember the CLI's stored credentials may permit sending or reading mail on your behalf — limit scopes where possible. If you cannot inspect gws or gws-shared, consider this an unknown-risk dependency and proceed cautiously.
